advice: Test a bounded B-panel layout inside gemm: for each contiguous block of up to 2*svcntsw() output columns, pack B into k-major storage with those columns contiguous, then reuse it across row tiles. Keep the existing four ZA output tiles and FP32 outer products; replace strided B loads with contiguous packed-panel loads. Allocate only n*panel_width floats, include allocation, packing, and free in the call, and retain a correct fallback if allocation fails. Handle the final short column panel with predicates and avoid reading or writing beyond n. This is a concrete layout hypothesis; the supplied evidence does not establish that it improves performance.
risks: Packing cost may exceed the saved B-load cost, especially because the packed panel is rebuilt for each column block. The benefit is unmeasured and may be within timing noise. Check n512 correctness against the frozen 0.002 tolerance, odd and short tails, n<=0, allocation failure behavior, and unchanged general GEMM ABI and FP32 arithmetic. Compare with a fresh AC baseline using repeated paired controls; do not attribute any joint result to this change alone.
